findings.text: follow-on: test_state_carries_the_stored_role_when_present asserts state["candidate"]["role"] == "measured" against the same literal "measured" the test passed in at line 840, so the two sides move together and the assertion holds whatever role value _signal_rerank_state writes, provided it writes the input through; it guards the key's presence, not that the stored role is carried from the candidate rather than fabricated, and a nearby independent check (line 849, role absent when the signal carries none) is what gives the pair any discriminating power.

follow-on: in test_role_search_narrows_the_vector_and_fulltext_streams the loop assertion params["role"] == "measured" (line 568) compares the bound parameter against the same role the test passed to _rank_signals, so it is not independent of the value under test; the companion assertion in the same loop that "signal_role = $role" appears in the query text is the independent half and the one that would redden on a dropped predicate, so this line adds little beyond a KeyError check.

follow-on: test_row_shows_the_stored_role_when_present asserts "Role: measured" in report against the same role="measured" it handed the fixture, so it round-trips the input rather than checking the formatter derives the role from the row's signal_role; the discriminating coverage is the sibling test at line 111, which supplies two distinct roles and asserts both appear, and that is where the regression guard actually rests.

item_verdicts.call_sites: production reach: the search_signals MCP tool at imas_codex/llm/server.py:2413 declares role= and forwards it to _search_signals at :2462; imas_codex/ids/slot_context.py:195 calls _vector_search_signals positionally with the new role defaulting to None, and imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:1083 calls _text_search_signals with the role defaulted off, both unaffected because role is keyword-defaulted; no test file counted.
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit over 6b4fcb5bb71717e304b87ff5f8d6cae97b64ad2e..1e2dc025211a84647099a9cf8647cb633fecc790; the single commit 1e2dc0252 changes six files — server.py, search_tools.py, domain_queries.py, the two llm test files and the new evidence fragment — adding role= to both query streams, the refusal, the rerank-state role and the covering tests, all inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names tests/llm/test_search_tools.py and tests/llm/test_signal_report_rows.py passing with the graph mocked; gate-head.log records 130 passed, 8 skipped, EXIT=0 at revision 6b4fcb5bb and negative-control.log records the declared mutation reddening the filter test at EXIT=1.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to let search_signals filter on a signal's stored role; imas_codex/llm/server.py:2413 adds role= to the tool, imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:388 refuses an out-of-set role, and the predicate is carried into both query streams, so the goal is met.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commit 1e2dc0252, gate 130 passed 8 skipped EXIT=0, negative_control_log negative-control.log, with the report-row item declared as pre-existing rendering that this node covered with tests rather than reimplemented.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares eight write paths; git diff 6b4fcb5bb..1e2dc0252 changes six files (server.py, search_tools.py, domain_queries.py, tests/llm/test_search_tools.py, tests/llm/test_signal_report_rows.py, ssfms-role-filter.html), every one inside the fence, while the declared search_formatters.py needed no change.

justifications.durability: the declared mutation — dropping the signal_role clause from signal_vector_search_block — reddens tests/llm/test_search_tools.py:550 (jt-60sa:ps/refip leaks into a role=measured result), so the filtered-search assertion is a genuine guard; the refusal and rerank-state assertions rest partly on literals the tests themselves pass in (lines 568, 844, 92), so the durability of the text-stream and rerank clauses is weaker than the vector clause the negative control covers.
justifications.evidence: gate-head.log:1 names the revision and command and records 130 passed, 8 skipped, EXIT=0, and negative-control.log:30 shows tests/llm/test_search_tools.py:550 reddening under the declared mutation; no baseline or after suite arm is recorded (both null on the reviewed run), and the filter is exercised only against a mocked graph, a caveat the fragment states at ssfms-role-filter.html:66.
justifications.fit: imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:98 derives SIGNAL_ROLES from the SignalRole enum and :388 follows the module's early-return refusal idiom, and the added names signal_role, SIGNAL_ROLES and _signal_rerank_state carry no plan, version or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:388 refuses a role outside SIGNAL_ROLES and the predicate reaches both the vector block (domain_queries.py:147) and the full-text branches (search_tools.py:825), so the filter is wired end to end; the report-row half of the deliverable is pre-existing rendering at search_formatters.py:186 that this node covered with tests rather than wrote.
justifications.reuse: the predicate is added to the existing owner signal_vector_search_block at imas_codex/graph/domain_queries.py:147 and the text clause reuses the same $role binding, while :98 reuses the SignalRole enum at imas_codex/graph/models.py:2338 rather than re-listing the six roles, so no capability is forked.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff 6b4fcb5bb..1e2dc0252 lists imas_codex/llm/server.py, imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py, imas_codex/graph/domain_queries.py, tests/llm/test_search_tools.py, tests/llm/test_signal_report_rows.py and docs/evidence/fragments/signal-search-finds-the-measured-signal/ssfms-role-filter.html, each inside the manifest's eight declared write paths, with no change to the out-of-scope surfaces.
